items.title: 10.9 Amount of substance produced during electrolysis

blocks.text: The value of F is used to calculate the mass of substance deposited at an electrode and the volume of gas produced at an electrode.
Sample Problem 10.5: lead from molten lead(II) bromide

Calculate the mass of lead deposited at the cathode when a current of 1.50 A flows through molten PbBr2 for 20.0 min (Ar of Pb 207; F = 96500 C mol-1). Step 1, the half-equation: Pb2+ + 2e- giving Pb. Step 2, the coulombs per mole of product: 2 moles of electrons per mole of Pb = 2F = 2 x 96500 = 193000 C mol-1. Step 3, the charge passed: Q = I x t = 1.50 x 20 x 60 = 1800 C. Step 4, the mass by proportion: 193000 C deposits 1 mole, 207 g, so 1800 C deposits 1800 / 193000 x 207 = 1.93 g of lead.

blocks.prompt: Silver nitrate solution is electrolysed for 35 min at 0.18 A. Find the mass of silver deposited (Ar 108). Then: 1.04 A for 6.00 min through dilute sulfuric acid gives 41.5 cm3 of hydrogen at STP; how many coulombs were passed, and how many liberate 1 mole of H2 (Quick Check 10.5)?
blocks.explanation: Silver: Q = 0.18 x 35 x 60 = 378 C; Ag+ needs 1 F, so mass = 378 / 96500 x 108 = 0.42 g. Hydrogen: Q = 1.04 x 360 = 374 C. 41.5 cm3 at STP is 41.5 / 22400 = 1.85 x 10^-3 mol, so 1 mole needs 374 / 1.85 x 10^-3 = 2.0 x 10^5 C, about 2F, as 2H+ + 2e- giving H2 requires.

items: Mass or gas volume from F: half-equation, charge per mole (nF), charge passed (It), proportion. Sample 10.5: 1.50 A for 20 min in PbBr2 gives 1800 C and 1.93 g Pb.
